title: Recursion basics
description: A function that calls itself — every recursion needs a base case to stop and a recursive case that shrinks the input toward it.

notes: Always write the base case FIRST — it is the easiest way to spot missing exits.
Each recursive call must move CLOSER to the base case, or you get infinite recursion → stack overflow.
Tail-call optimization is in the spec but NOT in V8/Node — deep recursion can still blow the stack. Prefer iteration for huge inputs.

questions.q: What happens if a recursive function has no base case?
options: It throws "Maximum call stack size exceeded"
The recursive call is the last thing the function does
There are exactly two recursive calls

questions.q: Does V8 / Node currently implement tail-call optimization?
questions.explain: The ES2015 spec allows it, but mainstream engines never shipped it.

exercises.prompt: Complete factorial with its base case and recursive step.
Recursive sum from n down to 0.

L3.prompt: Write `fib(n)` returning the nth Fibonacci number (fib(0)=0, fib(1)=1). Log `fib(10)`.
